limits.statement: A legacy missing result does not retain the source operationId. The decision graph reports operation.identity of a missing route as unknown (operation-id-missing-from-openapi) and lists the source id as a candidate only when the caller also passes the scan endpoint by endpoint key; without it the field has no candidates and authority none, while method and path keep their scan candidates.

Without the OpenAPI context audit a matched endpoint reports its request, response and error schemas as unknown (legacy-result-does-not-retain-none-vs-skipped-media-type), also for an operation that declares neither a request body nor responses. With the audit attached the same fields of the same operation are absent (request-body-absent, response-responses-absent, error-responses-absent). A caller of the graph alone cannot tell no schema from a skipped one.

An OpenAPI 3.0.3 document keeps operation identity, method and path of a matched endpoint, but its request, response and error schemas are skipped (unsupported-openapi-version). Schema projection is observed only for a 3.1.0 document; other OpenAPI versions were not run.

Without the audit, security that an operation inherits from the document stays unknown (root-security-inheritance-not-retained-by-legacy-result); with the audit it resolves as inherited-document-security. With the audit attached, a root requirement that names an undeclared scheme stays unknown (unknown-document-security-scheme) and a malformed root security value stays unknown (malformed-document-security).

When two operations of one document declare the same operationId, the graph built without the audit still reports a matched endpoint whose operation.identity is resolved to that id. With the audit the same document and endpoint give a conflict (duplicate-openapi-operation-id).

api.security.declared reports what the OpenAPI document declares (operation-explicitly-declared-public for security [], operation-security-requirements-declared for a named scheme). No fixture checks whether a runtime enforces it, so a declared requirement is not proof of enforcement.

A matched endpoint resolves only the fields the legacy reconciliation established: in the path-prefix fixture the graph counts resolved and unknown fields side by side (the pinned counts), so matched is not a verdict on the whole endpoint or on runtime behaviour.

No real runtime observation is recorded. The runtime binding, the evidence pair and the route observation in the fixtures are built by the test support module approved-evidence-fixture.mjs from constants (repeated-character hashes, a fixed attempt nonce, the repository repo/example, the revision abc123), not from a run. Runtime-backed promotion needs a T16 (beval) runtime binding and evidence pair from a run under an approved profile; this record has none.

The decision graph, the runtime route reconciliation and the promotion readiness report carry a 0-draft version, and the readiness report observed in readiness-source-spec-only has advisoryOnly true and stableCapabilityWire false. The vocabulary is not a frozen cross-track interface, and nothing recorded here is a stable capability or a certification claim.

The files listed under references, outside contracts/reconciliation-next and test/reconciliation-next, contain the text reconciliation-next at the base commit (recomputed with git grep): the CI workflow, the nested runner, the historical-replay scripts and fixture manifest, and the T19 acceptance records. The layer is referenced from outside its two directories.

The files listed under references hold an import line that names the layer (the historical-replay scripts, which use its evidence-binding and T16 runtime-evidence modules and the support module of the tests). No other file outside the two track directories matches the pattern at the base commit, so by this search contracts/openapi.mjs does not import the layer; an import with a computed path would not match.

The root test script is node --test test/*.test.mjs, which matches test files directly under test/ and not test/reconciliation-next. The suite runs through node scripts/run-next-nested-tests.mjs T09 (CI job nested-next) or through node --test on its test files (the direct-tap command), so a green root npm test is not T09 evidence.

The T19 acceptance records listed under references say that the evidence-binding regression tests of this layer run in the plain npm test lane. By the limit above the root test script does not match them, and no file under test/ other than the replay fixture manifest names the layer. The files belong to T19 and are not edited by this record; the claim is listed as it stands at the base commit.

The pinned modules import ajv and ajv-formats (through contracts/completeness.mjs and lib/schema-validate.mjs). The commands run in an extracted copy of the base commit whose node_modules is linked to the node_modules of the checkout that runs them (installed by npm ci). Before the link is made, the version of every package the pinned files import, and of the packages those require, is compared with the version the pinned package-lock.json states (environment.loaded_packages), and a difference fails the test. The scan of the imports is textual, so a specifier that is built at run time is not seen, and the files inside the installed packages are not hashed: only their versions are compared.

Only minimal hand-written OpenAPI documents, scan endpoints and support-module evidence are recorded. Behaviour on real application scans or real OpenAPI documents, and any performance or scale figure, is not recorded.
The recorded outputs, hashes and counts were generated on one machine (macOS arm64) with one Node major; other operating systems and architectures were not observed.

verification.recomputed: bytes, git_blob_sha1 and sha256 of every pinned file, per-file and total test counts, the exit code and counts of both commands, the first runner line, every fixture output hash and every expected value, the reference lists of the limits that carry them, the installed version of every package in environment.loaded_packages against package-lock.json at the base commit, and the per-file table, every test count, the NESTED_SUITE line and the base commit that the README and T09_STATUS.md state are compared by baseline-record.test.mjs with the values it recomputed, never with a copy kept in the documents.
levels: always: the record is well formed, and any single tampered hash, size, test count, exit code, expected value, limit status or commit id is reported; artifact_digest covers every field except its own value, so an edit of a limit statement, a fixture class, a call, a title or this text that is not re-sealed is reported

live files: size, sha256 and blob id are recomputed from the checkout; a file that disagrees in one hash or in size alone is damage and fails; a file that matches neither hash is drift, which skips the live replays while the pinned commit decides

pinned commit: the base commit is fetched once when absent and the sizes and digests of all pinned files, the runner included, are recomputed from its own blobs; if the commit is unavailable the test fails, and only BASELINE_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED=1 turns that into an explicit skip
ancestry: a shallow checkout is deepened with git fetch --no-tags --unshallow origin and the base commit must be an ancestor of HEAD

commands: both recorded commands are re-run in an extracted copy of the base commit (node_modules linked from the checkout once the installed versions equal environment.loaded_packages, which package-lock.json at the base commit states) and must reproduce exit code, counts, per-file counts and every fixture output
references: the files outside the track directories that match each recorded pattern are recomputed with git grep at the pinned commit and must equal the list in the limit

documents: the per-file table, every "<n> tests" figure, the NESTED_SUITE line and the base commit in README.md and T09_STATUS.md describe the pinned base commit and are compared with this record, whose counts and first runner line the commands level reproduces
not_recomputed: ci_observations: read once from the CI API (gh api, read-only) and kept for traceability; no test re-reads them
environment: describes the machine this record was generated on

prose: limit statements, fixture origins, the title and this text are bound only by artifact_digest, which reports an edit that is not re-sealed; an editor who re-seals the record is caught only by review of the diff and by the recomputed values above
the files inside the installed packages (ajv, ajv-formats and the packages they require): not hashed; only their versions are compared with package-lock.json at the base commit
support data: the runtime evidence in the fixtures is synthetic and built by approved-evidence-fixture.mjs; its values are not independently checked
README.md and T09_STATUS.md: only the numbers and the base commit named above are recomputed, not the explanatory text
